intro: The Andaman Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal, about 1,200 km from the mainland, and their beaches are the reason many people come. Most visitors split their time between Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), the capital, and the two islands a short ferry ride away: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), with Radhanagar and the main dive centres, and the smaller Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island).

The beaches range from long, lifeguarded public beaches to rocky coves and reef-fringed shores that come alive at low tide. This guide compares the best beaches on each island. For ferries, permits and a full itinerary, see our Andaman Islands travel guide.
quickAnswer: The best beaches in the Andaman Islands are Radhanagar (Beach No. 7) on Havelock for its long white sand and sunsets, Kalapathar and Elephant Beach on Havelock for sunrise and snorkelling, Laxmanpur and Bharatpur on Neil Island for sunset, rock formations and glass-bottom boats, and Corbyn's Cove and Chidiya Tapu near Port Blair. Visit from about November to April, and follow lifeguard flags and crocodile warnings.
takeaways: Radhanagar on Havelock is the Andamans' most famous beach and holds Blue Flag certification.
Elephant Beach (Havelock) and Bharatpur (Neil) are the main snorkelling and sea-walk beaches.
Laxmanpur on Neil is the sunset spot; Sitapur and Kalapathar are for sunrise.
Crocodiles live in some creeks and mangroves; swim only at recommended beaches.
The best months are about November to April; the monsoon brings rough seas and ferry cancellations.

items.name: Radhanagar Beach
body: A long curve of white sand backed by tall forest on Havelock's west coast, with lifeguards, changing rooms and a Blue Flag certification. The sea is calm and clear in season, and sunset draws a crowd. Check the current closing time; the beach is closed to visitors after dark.

image.caption: Radhanagar

items.name: Kalapathar Beach
body: A narrow beach on the east coast named after the black rocks along it, with turquoise water and a road running alongside. Best at sunrise.

items.name: Elephant Beach
body: Reached by speedboat from the jetty or a forest walk, Elephant Beach has a shallow reef close to shore for snorkelling, plus sea walks and other water activities. It gets busy by late morning.

items.name: Vijaynagar and Govind Nagar
body: The east-coast beaches numbered 3 and 5, where many resorts and dive centres stand. The sea goes out a long way at low tide, exposing rock pools.

items.name: Laxmanpur beaches
body: Laxmanpur 1 is a wide beach for sunset. Laxmanpur 2 leads, at low tide, to a natural rock arch often called the Howrah Bridge, with coral and sea life in the pools around it.

items.name: Bharatpur Beach
body: The beach next to Neil's jetty, with calm shallow water, snorkelling and glass-bottom boat rides.

items.name: Sitapur Beach
body: At the island's eastern tip, Sitapur faces the sunrise and has a rougher, more open sea.

links.label: Things to do on Neil Island

items.name: Corbyn's Cove
body: A small palm-fringed city beach a few kilometres from the centre, with water sports in season.

links.label: Things to do in Port Blair

items.name: Chidiya Tapu and Munda Pahar
body: At the southern tip of South Andaman, known for sunsets and birds; a forest trail leads to Munda Pahar beach.

items.name: North Bay and Jolly Buoy
body: Island beaches reached by boat, for coral viewing, snorkelling and sea walks. Jolly Buoy lies in a marine national park and opens in season only.

items.name: Lalaji Bay, Long Island
body: A quiet beach in Middle Andaman, reached by boat or a forest walk from Long Island village.

items.name: Ross and Smith islands
body: Two islands off Diglipur joined by a narrow sandbar, reached by boat with a forest department permit.

items.name: Kalipur
body: A North Andaman beach where sea turtles nest in season, near the start of the Saddle Peak trek.

items.name: Butler Bay, Little Andaman
body: A long, remote beach with surf in season, a long ferry ride south of Sri Vijaya Puram.

sections.heading: How many days?
paras: Five to seven nights is ideal: one or two in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), three on Havelock and one or two on Neil. With four nights, skip Neil or do it as a day trip. Add days for diving courses or trips to North Andaman.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: From about November to April the sea is calmer, the water clearer and ferries more reliable, with December and January the busiest months. The south-west monsoon, from about May or June to September, brings heavy rain, rough seas and ferry cancellations, and beach swimming is often restricted. October and May are shoulder months with some rain.

sections.heading: Planning a beach trip
list: Fly into Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) and take a ferry to Havelock and Neil; book ferries early for December and January.
Allow at least two nights on Havelock and one on Neil, plus a night in Sri Vijaya Puram.
Beaches such as Radhanagar and Elephant Beach have fixed opening hours and close by early evening.
Cash is useful on the islands; card and network coverage can be patchy.
after: For diving, kayaking, treks and the Baratang caves, see adventure activities in the Andamans.

safety: Swim only at beaches with lifeguards, inside the flagged zone, and never when a red flag is up or during the monsoon.
Saltwater crocodiles live in some creeks and mangroves; obey warning signs and never swim at dusk or in creek mouths.
Wear footwear on rocky and coral stretches such as Laxmanpur 2; coral cuts easily infect.
Do not touch, stand on or collect coral and shells; it is illegal and damages the reef.
Avoid swimming in rough seas and during the monsoon, even at lifeguarded beaches.
Respect the rules in tribal reserves on the road north: no stopping, photos or contact.

faqs.q: Which is the best beach in the Andaman Islands?
faqs.a: Radhanagar Beach on Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) is the best known, for its long white sand, calm sea in season and sunsets.

faqs.q: Which Andaman beach is best for snorkelling?
faqs.a: Elephant Beach on Havelock and Bharatpur on Neil, plus North Bay and Jolly Buoy near Sri Vijaya Puram.

faqs.q: Is it safe to swim in the Andamans?
faqs.a: At lifeguarded beaches such as Radhanagar, in calm conditions and within flags, yes. Avoid creeks and mangroves because of crocodiles.

faqs.q: Which is better for beaches, Havelock or Neil?
faqs.a: Havelock has more famous beaches and diving; Neil is smaller, quieter and good for rock formations and a slower pace. Most people visit both.
